title: Novo Nordisk starts trialing lower maintenance doses of oral Wegovy
snippet: The Phase 3 study is evaluating two doses of Novo’s Wegovy pill in people with obesity or overweight in combination with a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity.

title: Roche pours $750M into Oregon manufacturing plant as obesity push expands
snippet: After committing $2 billion to a new North Carolina facility to boost capacity for its next-gen obesity candidates, Roche's Genentech is putting down more cash to expand a device fill-finish site in Oregon.

title: Scribe’s early-stage IPO standout defies biotech’s derisking trend
snippet: Scribe Therapeutics’ one-time epigenetic treatment is designed to slash the adherence burden of chronic cholesterol-lowering therapies while sidestepping the irreversibility of gene editing.

title: Regeneron wins FDA approval to challenge Ipsen for rare bone disease market
snippet: Regeneron’s Pasatru is the second fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva drug approved in the U.S., following the 2023 approval of Ipsen’s Sohonos.

title: Ultragenyx bags first gene therapy approval as previously rejected Sanfilippo asset awaits decision
snippet: The accelerated greenlight for Ultragenyx’s gene therapy for glycogen storage disease has raised analyst expectations for approval of UX111, which the FDA rejected last summer and is currently reviewing for a second time. A decision is expected by mid-September.

title: Merck’s Moderna-partnered vaccine success clears view of post-Keytruda future
snippet: Investors had been pessimistic about the probability of success for the personalized cancer vaccine intismeran autogene, so the Phase 3 win was a welcome surprise.

title: Rewriting the rules of CMV prevention
snippet: In this episode of Denatured, you’ll hear from Ian McGowan, Chief Medical Officer at Synklino and James Hunter, associate professor of transplantation at Oxford University. We explore transplantation and antiviral innovation and why CMV remains one of the most persistent and consequential challenges facing transplant...

title: 7 biopharma M&A deals where layoffs followed
snippet: Workforce cuts this year at seven companies involved in recent mergers and acquisitions will cost over 1,300 employees their jobs. Affected businesses include Arcellx and Tourmaline Bio, acquired by Gilead Sciences and Novartis, respectively.

title: Out of sight, out of work? What’s driving remote job cuts
snippet: Biopharma professionals sometimes find themselves out of jobs when employers want to bring staff back into the office, as recently seen at biotech EMD Serono and Exelixis.

title: Why pediatric rare oncology outperforms in a volatile biotech market
snippet: Real progress happens where unmet medical need is greatest and patient impact can be clearly measured. Pediatric rare cancers exemplify these criteria and have therefore generated continued investment, even in a capital-constrained environment.

title: Trump's FDA pick Overton good for psychedelics, new pain meds but bad for vaccines: Analysts
snippet: If confirmed by the Senate, Heidi Overton—officially revealed Wednesday as President Donald Trump’s choice for FDA commissioner—is expected to be a boon for developers of psychedelic therapeutics and non-opioid pain drugs, but could tow the party line on vaccines.

title: Kolon TissueGene cuts 37 US staffers after Phase 3 fail
snippet: Follow along as BioSpace tracks job cuts and restructuring initiatives.

title: 11 companies hiring in New Jersey
snippet: Looking for a biopharma job in New Jersey? Job postings in the area have increased year over year, according to BioSpace data. Here are 11 companies with open roles.

title: Moderna stock nearly doubles as Merck-partnered mRNA cancer vaccine meets Phase 3 goal
snippet: Melanoma was slower to recur in patients receiving Merck and Moderna's mRNA vaccine with Keytruda, supporting use of the combination in adjuvant treatment. The partners plan to take the data to the FDA.

title: Trump picks White House aide Heidi Overton as FDA chief: Reports
snippet: If Heidi Overton clears the Senate nomination process, analysts say she will have a tough job ahead to “restore predictability” to an agency battered by layoffs and controversial policies.

title: Enveda’s exercise-simulating obesity tablet clears early clinical test
snippet: Touting an “exceptional” gastrointestinal safety profile for its oral obesity drug candidate in a study of healthy volunteers, Enveda plans to test the asset in people stopping GLP-1 treatment.

title: 2026 IPO stock tracker: How newly public biotechs are performing
snippet: BioSpace is launching an IPO dashboard to help the industry keep tabs on U.S. biotechs that have taken the public plunge in 2026.

title: Amylyx’s redemption story, Summit’s survival woes, Definium’s anxiety win, more
snippet: Amylyx shares good news for its investigational GLP-1 blocker; Definium announces positive data for its LSD-based therapy in anxiety; Summit/Akeso’s ivonescimab shows degrading survival benefits; patients treated with Neurocrine’s Prader-Willi drug experience serious adverse events; and Eli Lilly cracks down on the bl...

title: Leadership Lab: The one person executives need by their side
snippet: An executive who is rarely short on ideas needs someone to pull their big ideas through to implementation. Kaye/Bassman’s Michael Pietrack explains why this person, who he calls the implementer, may be the most important hire in the building.

title: Takeda leads wave of orexin drugs with potential to upend narcolepsy market
snippet: The FDA’s August approval of Takeda’s Orzeyful for treating the full set of narcolepsy symptoms initiated a new era in the sleep market.

title: Chaotic adcomms threaten to derail FDA’s bid to renew trust after Makary, Prasad
snippet: The FDA has been trying to mend fences with rare disease drug developers and patient groups since the departure of former Commissioner Marty Makary three months ago. But advisory committee meetings last week for Replimune and Capricor Therapeutics only created more confusion and frustration.

title: Biotech’s China problem: An issue of national security or economic value for the US?
snippet: Congressional letters sent to the CEOs of Eli Lilly, Pfizer, Merck, BMS and AbbVie this week voicing concerns about the pharmas' clinical trials in China highlight an ongoing discrepancy in how government and industry think about the rise of the Asian country’s biotech industry.

title: BIO 2026: Cell and gene therapy sector must break the mold to thrive
snippet: If cell and gene therapy makers are going to achieve their mission to improve patients’ lives, the industry must come together to share information across stakeholders, from regulators to manufacturers to payers.

title: At FDA, ‘caretaker mode’ is better than power trip mode
snippet: UniQure’s planned third-quarter submission for its Huntington’s disease gene therapy may be a harbinger of a more flexible FDA under acting commissioner Kyle Diamantas—but how long will it last? And how can companies be sure these positive decisions won’t just be reversed?
